messages.author: e08e85a0d7624556
messages.subject: Trouble using ordinal endogenous variable
parts:
Hello,

I am new to R and trying to use lavaan to estimate a SEM with an ordinal endogenous variable.
The instructions on the website here (http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html) suggest that if I run the model with my variable declared as ordered lavaan will automatically switch to the WLSMV estimator, however, I used the following and got the following error message:

semmodel <- ' 
+ #measurement model
+ nhd.qual  =~ nhd_qal_envt_RV + nhd_qal_bldgs_RV + nhd_qal_quiet_RV + nhd_qal_park_RV      
+ soc.contact =~ cntct_rel_RV + cntct_frnd_RV + cntct_nbr_RV
+ wemwbs =~ wemwbs_optim + wemwbs_useful + wemwbs_relax + wemwbs_intrstdpeople + wemwbs_energy + wemwbs_dealprob + wemwbs_thinkclear + wemwbs_goodself + wemwbs_close + wemwbs_confident + wemwbs_makemind + wemwbs_loved + wemwbs_intrstdthings + wemwbs_cheerful
+ nhd.problms.incivil =~nhd_prblm_violence_RC + nhd_prblm_insulted_RC + nhd_prblm_racism_RC + nhd_prblm_drugs_RC + nhd_prblm_alchl_RC + nhd_prblm_gangs_RC + nhd_prblm_teen_loiter_RC + nhd_prblm_nbr_nuisance_RC + nhd_prblm_burglary_RC
+ nhd.problms.env =~nhd_prblm_litter_RC + nhd_prblm_derelict_RC + nhd_prblm_vandalism_RC + nhd_prblm_air_RC + nhd_prblm_traffic_RC
+ qual.local.amen =~loc_serv_fruit_veg_w3_RV + loc_serv_venues_RV + loc_serv_shops_RV + loc_serv_shops_RV
+ qual.local.srv =~ loc_serv_pavmnt_w3_RV + loc_serv_light_w3_RV + loc_serv_transpt_RV + loc_serv_strt_cln_RV + loc_serv_police_RV
+ 
+ #regressions
+ wemwbs ~ soc.contact + nhd.qual + nhd.problms.incivil + nhd.problms.env + qual.local.amen + qual.local.srv + nhd_walk_20min_cont + resp_sex + adlt_lt_phys_cardioresp + amenity_use_non_retail_local + Age80_plus + Age70_79 + adlt_lt_muscskel + wlk_dark_RV + vehicle_RC + live_alone'
> 
> fit <- sem(semmodel, data=mydata)


Error in lavaan::lavaan(model = semmodel, data = mydata, model.type = "sem",  : 
  lavaan ERROR: estimator ML for ordered data is not supported yet. Use WLSMV instead.
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: exogenous variable(s) declared as ordered in data: nhd_walk_20min_cont

I then used the ordered argument when fitting the model and got the following:

fit <- sem(semmodel, data=mydata, ordered=c("nhd_walk_20min_cont"))

Error in lavsamplestats@cov[[g]][cbind(row.idx, col.idx)] : 
  subscript out of bounds
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: exogenous variable(s) declared as ordered in data: nhd_walk_20min_cont
2: In lav_partable_check(lavpartable, categorical = categorical, warn = TRUE) :
  lavaan WARNING: parameter table does not contain thresholds



I then tried to change the estimator to WLSMV manually and it ran, but then the output still says estimator: ML and I get the following warning messages:

fit <- sem(semmodel, data=mydata, estimator="WLSMV")

lavaan (0.5-18) converged normally after 107 iterations

                                                  Used       Total
  Number of observations                          1093        1107

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic             4369.565
  Degrees of freedom                              1259
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: exogenous variable(s) declared as ordered in data: nhd_walk_20min_cont
2: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble inverting W matrix; used generalized inverse


If anybody can help me understand whether I am doing something wrong in the first place meaning lavaan does not automatically switch to the WLSMV estimator and secondly whether I can be confident the output is correct when I used WLSMV, even though it says it's still ML and what the warning messages mean, would be greatly appreciated. 


Thanks

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Trouble using ordinal endogenous variable
parts:
The only ordinal variable you appear to have nhd_walk_20min_cont, which is not an indicator or endogenous outcome of any kind in your model.  It is merely an exogenous predictor, so no assumptions about its distribution need to be made.  But unlike regression functions (e.g., lm, lme, or glm), lavaan will not automatically create dummy codes for factor variables (ordered or otherwise).  So you just have to make your own dummy codes and include those as predictors of wemwbs instead.

Terry
